==Description==
[[File:Melothria scabra florescence.jpg|thumb|left|''Melothria scabra'' female flower]]
''Melothria scabra'' is a [[vine]] similar in [[Morphology (biology)|morphology]] to ''[[Melothria pendula]]''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Woodson|first1=Robert E.|last2=Schery|first2=Robert W.|last3=Wunderlin|first3=Richard P.|date=1978|title=Flora of Panama. Part IX. Family 182. Cucurbitaceae|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2395357|journal=Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden|volume=65|issue=1|pages=285–366|doi=10.2307/2395357|jstor=2395357 |issn=0026-6493|url-access=subscription}}</ref> It has a climbing [[Habit (biology)|habit]], and typically grows {{convert|2.5-3|m|ft|1|abbr=on}} tall.<ref name=":0" /> It is fast growing:<ref name=":0" /> [[germination]] under favourable conditions takes approximately 10 days, with plants reaching maturity in approximately 60–75 days.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Rice|first1=Emily|last2=Curtis|first2=Kynda R.|date=2021|title=Drought-Tolerant Options for Southwest Agriculture: Edible Produce|url=https://core.ac.uk/display/428380291|language=en-gb}}</ref> It is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] species, but as it is not [[Hardiness (plants)|frost hardy]] it is often grown as an [[Annual plant|annual]].<ref name=":0" /> Its [[Leaf|leaves]] have three or five lobes, and are {{Convert|3-7|cm|in|1|abbr=on}} in length and width.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=Melothria scabra Naudin|url=http://worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-0000377170|access-date=2021-06-20|website=worldfloraonline.org}}</ref> The [[Glossary of leaf morphology|leaf margin]] is undulate or dentate, the apex is caudate, and the leaf base is cordate.<ref name=":6" /> The leaf surface is [[Glossary of botanical terms|scabrous]]; the upper surface is covered with small hairs called [[Trichome|trichomes]].<ref name=":6" /> Similar to some types of cucumber,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pawełkowicz|first1=Magdalena Ewa|last2=Skarzyńska|first2=Agnieszka|last3=Pląder|first3=Wojciech|last4=Przybecki|first4=Zbigniew|date=2019-03-13|title=Genetic and molecular bases of cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) sex determination|journal=Molecular Breeding|language=en|volume=39|issue=3|pages=50|doi=10.1007/s11032-019-0959-6|issn=1572-9788|doi-access=free}}</ref> these plants are [[Plant reproductive morphology|monoecious]], producing both male ([[Stamen|staminate]]) and female ([[Gynoecium|pistillate]]) [[Flower|flowers]] on the same plant.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Melothria L.|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:30043481-2|access-date=2021-06-21|website=Plants of the World Online|publisher=Kew Science}}</ref> Flowers are small and yellow, and are approximately {{Convert|4|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} in diameter.<ref name=":0" /> Unusually for the cucurbits, the female flowers appear before the male flowers.<ref name=":3" /> These plants can [[Pollination|pollinate]] themselves, but the individual flowers are [[Self-incompatibility|not self-fertile]].  Each plant can produce hundreds of fruits,<ref name=":5" /> which develop at the base of the female flowers (the [[Ovary (botany)|ovaries]] are inferior).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Melothria scabra|url=https://plantdatabase.kpu.ca/plant/plantDetail/1774|access-date=2021-06-20|website=Kwantlen Polytechnic University School of Horticulture Plant Database}}</ref> Fruits are [[olive]]-shaped,<ref name=":0" /> grow to {{Convert|2.5-4|cm|in|1|abbr=on}} in length, and {{Convert|1.5-2.5|cm|in|1|abbr=on}} in width, and are green with dark green stripes.<ref name=":1" /> In contrast to the fruits of most other wild species in the cucurbit family, the fruit of ''Melothria scabra'' has a sweet rather than bitter flesh.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Chomicki|first1=Guillaume|last2=Schaefer|first2=Hanno|last3=Renner|first3=Susanne S.|date=2020|title=Origin and domestication of Cucurbitaceae crops: insights from phylogenies, genomics and archaeology|journal=New Phytologist|language=en|volume=226|issue=5|pages=1240–1255|doi=10.1111/nph.16015|pmid=31230355 |issn=1469-8137|doi-access=free}}</ref> Plants are drought resistant and pest-resistant relative to other cucumbers.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news
| last = Spurrier
| first = Jeff
| title = Mouse melon, a.k.a. Mexican gherkin: Tiny fruit is big on cute
| newspaper = LA Times
| date = 2013-05-14
|url=https://www.latimes.com/home/la-lh-mouse-melons-mexican-gherkins-20130514-story.html
}}</ref>

==Etymology==

=== Binomial name ===
The genus name ''{{linktext|Melothria}}'' is from Ancient Greek μηλοθρων: mēlothrōn 'kind of white grape' in reference to small grapevine fruits born by the genus. The [[specific epithet]] ''{{wikt-lang|la|scabra}}'' is [[Latin]] for 'rough, scabby'''.''

=== Common names ===
The [[English language]] common name 'cucamelon' arose in the 1980s; it is a [[portmanteau]] of 'cucumber' and '[[melon]]'.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020|title=Definition of cucamelon|url=https://www.lexico.com/definition/cucamelon|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304063203/https://www.lexico.com/definition/cucamelon|archive-date=March 4, 2021|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-20|website=Lexico.com|publisher=Oxford University Press}}</ref> The [[Spanish language]] common name '{{wikt-lang|es|sandita}}<nowiki/>' translates as 'little watermelon';<ref name=":2" /> its etymology is {{wikt-lang|es|sandía}} 'watermelon' + ''ita'', a [[suffix]] used to indicate something is small.<ref>{{Cite web|title=English Translation of "sandía"|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/spanish-english/sand%C3%ADa|access-date=2021-06-20|website=Collins Spanish-English Dictionary|publisher=HarperCollins Publishers}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020|title=Translation of "-ito" into English|url=https://www.lexico.com/es-en/traducir/-ito|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200814081811/https://www.lexico.com/es-en/traducir/-ito|archive-date=August 14, 2020|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-20|website=Lexico.com|publisher=Oxford University Press}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Melothria scabra'' is [[Native species|native]] to [[Colombia]], [[El Salvador]], [[Guatemala]], [[Honduras]], Mexico,{{efn-lr|In Mexico, ''Melothria scabra'' is native to the following [[World Geographical Scheme for Recording Plant Distributions|WGSRPD]] level-3 floristic units: Mexico Central, Mexico Northeast, Mexico Northwest, Mexico Southeast, and Mexico Southwest.<ref name="POWO"/>}} [[Nicaragua]], [[Panama]], and Venezuela,<ref name="POWO"/> where it grows in [[Forest|forests]] and [[Thicket|thickets]].<ref name=":1" />

== Diseases ==
''Melothria scabra'' is susceptible to [[infection]] by ''[[Pseudoperonospora cubensis]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Wilson|first=Guy West|date=1908|title=Studies in North American Peronosporales-IV. Host Index|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2479110|journal=Bulletin of the Torrey Botanical Club|volume=35|issue=11|pages=543–554|doi=10.2307/2479110|jstor=2479110 |issn=0040-9618|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Ellett|first=C. Wayne|date=1970|title=Annotated List of the Personosporales of Ohio (I. Albuginaceae and Peronosporaceae)|url=https://core.ac.uk/display/76294860|language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Ellett|first=C. Wayne|date=1989|title=Ohio plant disease index|url=https://core.ac.uk/display/159595750|language=en-gb}}</ref> a [[Plant pathology|plant pathogen]] that causes cucurbit downy mildew.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Savory|first1=Elizabeth A.|last2=Granke|first2=Leah L.|last3=Quesada-Ocampo|first3=Lina M.|last4=Varbanova|first4=Marina|last5=Hausbeck|first5=Mary K.|last6=Day|first6=Brad|date=2011|title=The cucurbit downy mildew pathogen Pseudoperonospora cubensis|journal=Molecular Plant Pathology|language=en|volume=12|issue=3|pages=217–226|doi=10.1111/j.1364-3703.2010.00670.x|issn=1364-3703|pmc=6640371|pmid=21355994}}</ref> It is also susceptible to infection by another plant pathogen, ''[[Podosphaera fuliginea|Podosphaera xanthii]]'', which causes [[powdery mildew]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rennberger|first1=G.|last2=Kousik|first2=C. S.|last3=Keinath|first3=A. P.|date=2017-09-06|title=First Report of Powdery Mildew on Cucumis zambianus, Cucurbita digitata, and Melothria scabra Caused by Podosphaera xanthii in the United States|journal=Plant Disease|volume=102|issue=1|pages=246|doi=10.1094/PDIS-06-17-0916-PDN|issn=0191-2917|doi-access=free}}</ref> Plants are reported to be susceptible to infection by ''[[Cucumber mosaic virus]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Price|first=W. C.|date=1940|title=Comparative Host Ranges of Six Plant Viruses|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2437088|journal=American Journal of Botany|volume=27|issue=7|pages=530–541|doi=10.2307/2437088|jstor=2437088 |issn=0002-9122|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
[[File:Cucamelons.JPG|thumb|168x168px|Melothria scabra fruits.]]
''Melothria scabra'' is cultivated as a minor [[crop]] for its fruits,<ref name=":4" /> which are eaten raw or [[Pickling|pickled]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Watson|first=Sereno|date=1886|title=Contributions to American Botany|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25129875|journal=Proceedings of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences|volume=22|pages=396–481|doi=10.2307/25129875|jstor=25129875 |issn=0199-9818|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
